title: Four Astronauts, Four Pixels: The Coolest Blurry Photo Ever!
summary: Have you ever taken a photo that came out super blurry? Maybe you moved the camera, or the thing you were photographing was just too far away. Well, scientists just took the blurriest—and maybe the coolest—photo ever! It shows a handful of black-and-white pixels. But those pixels are actually four astronauts zooming around the moon at 2,000 miles per hour. That's as fast as a speeding bullet! The picture was snapped by the Green Bank Telescope in West Virginia. This telescope is huge—its dish is as wide as a football field! It was pointing at the Artemis II capsule, nicknamed Integrity, when it was 213,000 miles away. That's like stacking 30 Earths on top of each other. The photo shows radio waves from the capsule, not regular light. When astronomer Will Armentrout first saw it, he said, 'There are four people in those pixels.' And he was right! The crew—Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen—were on a historic trip around the moon. They traveled farther from Earth than any humans ever before. So next time your photo is blurry, don't delete it. It might just be a record-breaker!
why_it_matters: Even a blurry photo can show something amazing, like astronauts traveling farther than ever before — next time you snap a blurry picture, maybe it’s capturing a world record!

keywords.explanation: Pixels are tiny dots of color that make up a digital picture; when you zoom in, you can see them like little squares.
Astronauts are people who travel into space in rockets and capsules to explore places like the moon.
The Green Bank Telescope is a gigantic dish in West Virginia that listens to radio waves from space.
Artemis II is a NASA mission that sent a crew of four astronauts on a trip around the moon.
Radio waves are invisible energy that can carry signals through space, like how a car radio picks up music.
An astronomer is a scientist who studies stars, planets, and other things in space using telescopes.

perspectives.description: He was amazed and proud that the radio telescope could detect the capsule with its crew so far away, calling it a historic image.
On first glance, a blurry black-and-white image seems like a mistake, but with context it becomes exciting.
The crew likely felt a sense of pride knowing that even from 213,000 miles away, people on Earth could 'see' them through radio waves.
